sub_graphs.name: DAS Core Types
sub_graphs.description: Custom types used across the DAS specification for indexing rows, columns, and custody groups in the extended data matrix.

state_variables.name: RowIndex
state_variables.description: Row identifier in the matrix of cells.

state_variables.name: ColumnIndex
state_variables.description: Column identifier in the matrix of cells.

state_variables.name: CustodyIndex
state_variables.description: Custody group identifier in the set of custody groups.

sub_graphs.name: DAS Constants and Configuration
sub_graphs.description: Non-configurable constants and configurable parameters governing the DAS system including matrix dimensions, custody groups, and sampling parameters.

invariants.text: UINT256_MAX equals uint256(2**256 - 1), used as an overflow boundary.
NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS equals CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (= 128), defining the fixed width of the extended data matrix.
NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS is 128, the total number of custody groups available.
CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT is 4, the minimum number of custody groups an honest node must custody.
SAMPLES_PER_SLOT is 8, the minimum number of samples for an honest node per slot.

sub_graphs.name: DAS Container Definitions
sub_graphs.description: SSZ container definitions for DataColumnSidecar (used for column gossip and storage) and MatrixEntry (used for matrix computation and reconstruction).

sub_graphs.name: get_custody_groups Helper
sub_graphs.description: Deterministic, public function that computes which custody groups a node is responsible for, based on the node's ID and the desired custody group count. Uses hash-based pseudo-random selection.

invariants.text: The returned custody groups list has exactly custody_group_count unique elements.
The returned list is sorted in ascending order.
Increasing custody_group_count for a given node_id extends (rather than reshuffles) the returned list.
The function is deterministic: same inputs always produce same outputs.

functions.signature: def get_custody_groups(node_id: NodeID, custody_group_count: uint64) -> Sequence[CustodyIndex]
functions.description: Returns a sorted list of unique CustodyIndex values pseudo-randomly derived from node_id. If custody_group_count == NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS, returns all groups without computation.

post_conditions.text: All elements in result are unique (len(result) == len(set(result)))
Result is sorted in ascending order

sub_graphs.name: compute_columns_for_custody_group Helper
sub_graphs.description: Computes the set of column indices that belong to a given custody group. Uses interleaved mapping: columns_per_group = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS / NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS, with column = NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group.

invariants.text: Each custody group maps to exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS // NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS columns.
The union of all custody group column sets covers all NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS columns exactly once (partition property).

functions.description: Returns the list of ColumnIndex values assigned to the given custody group via interleaved mapping.

post_conditions.text: All returned column indices are in range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS)

sub_graphs.name: compute_matrix Helper
sub_graphs.description: Computes the full extended data matrix from a sequence of blobs. Each blob is expanded via compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs into cells and proofs, then flattened into MatrixEntry objects indexed by (row=blob_index, column=cell_index).

invariants.text: The matrix has exactly len(blobs) * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS entries.
Each MatrixEntry's row_index corresponds to the originating blob index and column_index to the cell index.

functions.description: Returns the full flattened sequence of MatrixEntry by computing cells and KZG proofs for each blob.

post_conditions.text: Each entry has valid cell, kzg_proof, column_index, and row_index

sub_graphs.name: recover_matrix Helper
sub_graphs.description: Recovers the full data matrix from a partial matrix using erasure coding recovery. For each blob row, collects available cells and applies recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs to reconstruct all cells.

invariants.text: Recovery requires at least 50% of columns per row to succeed.
The recovered matrix has exactly blob_count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS entries.

functions.signature: def recover_matrix(partial_matrix: Sequence[MatrixEntry], blob_count: uint64) -> Sequence[MatrixEntry]
functions.description: Recovers the full flattened matrix from a partial matrix by applying erasure coding recovery per blob row.

pre_conditions.text: partial_matrix contains at least 50% of columns for each row (blob) to enable recovery.

post_conditions.text: All recovered cells and proofs are valid and consistent with the original blob data.

sub_graphs.name: Custody Protocol Rules
sub_graphs.description: Behavioral requirements for nodes participating in the DAS custody protocol, including custody obligations, sampling behavior, reconstruction, and cross-seeding.

invariants.text: Nodes custodying a custody group MUST custody all columns in that group.
When syncing, a node MUST backfill columns from all of its custody groups.
Custody selection is public and deterministic via get_custody_groups.
A node stores custodied columns for the duration of the pruning period.
Sampling is successful if the node retrieves all selected columns.
sampling_size = max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count) for each slot.
If a node obtains 50%+ of all columns, it SHOULD reconstruct the full matrix via recover_matrix.
After reconstruction, nodes MUST expose new columns as if received over the network.
If subscribed to the subnet of a reconstructed column, the node MUST send the DataColumnSidecar to mesh neighbors.

sub_graphs.name: Modified is_data_available
sub_graphs.description: Modified data availability check for Fulu that replaces blob retrieval with column sidecar retrieval and verification. Uses retrieve_column_sidecars to get all column sidecars to sample, then verifies each with verify_data_column_sidecar and verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs.

invariants.text: Data is considered available only if ALL column sidecars pass both structural verification and KZG proof verification.
The p2p network does not guarantee sidecar retrieval outside of MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs.
This function replaces the previous blob-based data availability check with column-sidecar-based verification (EIP-7594).

functions.description: Returns True if all column sidecars for the given block root are retrievable and pass verification (both structural and KZG proof). Replaces blob-based check from prior forks.

pre_conditions.text: beacon_block_root must reference a known block.

post_conditions.text: Returns True only if retrieve_column_sidecars succeeds AND all sidecars pass verify_data_column_sidecar AND verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs.
Returns False or raises exception if any column sidecar is missing or fails verification.

sub_graphs.name: Modified on_block Handler
sub_graphs.description: Fork choice handler invoked upon receiving a new block. Modified in Fulu (EIP-7594) to call is_data_available without blob_kzg_commitments as input. Validates the block against the store, checks data availability, executes state transition, and updates checkpoints.

invariants.text: Parent block must be known in store.block_states.
Block slot must not be in the future (get_current_slot(store) >= block.slot).
Block slot must be after the finalized epoch slot.
Block must be a descendant of the finalized checkpoint block.
Data must be available via is_data_available(hash_tree_root(block)) -- modified in Fulu to use column sidecars.
State transition must succeed (block is valid).

functions.signature: def on_block(store: Store, signed_block: SignedBeaconBlock) -> None
functions.description: Processes a new block: validates parent existence, timing, finality, data availability (via column sidecars in Fulu), runs state transition, and updates store with new block state and checkpoints.

post_conditions.text: store.block_states[block_root] contains the post-state after state_transition.
Block timeliness is recorded via record_block_timeliness.
Checkpoints updated if necessary via update_checkpoints.
Unrealized justification and finality computed via compute_pulled_up_tip.
